findings: AgentRegistry.setFactory() holds exactly one factory slot; a second registration throws.
AgentRegistry.create()/resume() delegate to the registered factory.
AgentRegistry.register(agent) records an already-constructed agent as a runtime root and awaits serial agent/created dispatch.
AgentRegistry.enter(agent, owner) rejects id collision and id/session.id mismatch; returns an idempotent detach closure.
Custom coordinators must use register()/enter(), never a second setFactory().
The runtime Agent interface (module augmentation of ./types.ts) requires: id, options, session, inbox, status, ctx, cancel(), whenIdle(), runMaintenance(), send(), followup(), steer(), inject().
Never await whenIdle() from an agent/created listener.
Session.append(type, data, ...surfaceOpts) builds the envelope { type, seq, time, data } and validates data via validateSessionEventData.

SessionEventMap is merge-extensible via 'declare module' augmentation; scripts/gen-persistence-catalog.ts scans every SessionEventMap merge, so system1/* declarations become KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES when the catalog is regenerated.

system1/* events are REQUIRED (no ignorable marker): they carry decision/budget/attempt state whose loss would corrupt replay. Sessions driven by the coordinator require a system1-aware build to restore; rollback keeps the package loaded and switches mode to off/shadow instead of removing it.
ToolRuntime is a Cordis Service ('tools'); ToolRuntime.execute(ToolExecutionInput) is the public guarded entry point running the full pre/guard/around/post/result pipeline.
ToolExecutionInput: { callId, rootCallId?, name, schema?, arguments, agent?, parent?, signal } (signal is required, caller-owned).
The TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER symbol view is @internal, not a plugin extension point; the adapter uses execute().
